# Evening handover: river monitoring station

The battery was replaced at 16:20. The new unit passed the load test, and the logger resumed sending readings before the end of the shift. Leave the spare battery on the upper shelf until the supplier confirms whether it needs another inspection. The cabinet key is in the labelled envelope beside the radio.

The instruments near the bridge has been checked twice today. Both sets of readings agree with the manual gauge. There is no reason to change the alarm threshold yet, although the overnight forecast includes more rain. If the river rises above the painted marker, call the duty officer and record the time in the paper log as well as the shared file.

Please remember to seperate the damaged cables from the working ones. A yellow tag means that a cable needs testing; it does not mean that the cable can be thrown away. We have fewer equipment than we expected, so keeping a clear inventory will help the morning crew decide what to bring.

The station computer still shows yesterday’s map. Refreshing the browser did not resolve the problem. An engineer will inspect the cache settings tomorrow; until then, use the printed map on the wall. The labels on that copy were checked last week and remain correct.

I have left a flask of hot water in the kitchen. Please empty it before you leave and switch off the small heater under the desk. The main cabinet must remain powered overnight. Write any unexpected noise or flashing lights in the log, even if the readings look normal. A short description of what you noticed is more useful than a guess about the cause.
